workflow_instructions.mode_overview: This mode turns a written requirement, or screenshots of the screens, into a running BAW process app with no Process Designer work. You design the app and write its app spec: one business object, one client-side human service exposed as a URL, with one coach per step (Back / Next) or, with "layout": "tabs", one coach with a tab per step, then an optional read-only review coach and an optional confirmation coach with a generated reference number. With a "process" section the form becomes the first task of a workflow with lanes, and an optional approval task (Approve / Send Back) follows in a second lane (or a plain review task). With a "database" section the form task also loads and saves a row of a PostgreSQL table in bawexternal (a Load button, and a save on Submit); the database tools (list_tables, describe_table, run_sql, export_table, import_table, change_system_db) let you look at the data and build the table (the baw-database skill). The baw-dev-tools MCP server builds its coaches from App Builder Widgets (the ABW toolkit: Theme, App Header, Section, Review List, Button Bar), so authors can rearrange them by drag and drop in Coach Designer, then installs and tests it. When the user asks for a React + Carbon UI, you hand the app to the BAW Coach Modernizer mode.

step.details: When the switch reason names an app, change its app spec (work/ACR.app.json) as asked and continue at the design stop. Keep its acronym and theme file, bump app.snapshot, and pass the installed app's acronym as create_app base. The new snapshot has no "(Modernized)" services, so after it is installed and tested, offer to switch back to BAW Coach Modernizer to generate them again; when the user already asked for that, switch back without asking. In the reason, give the new snapshot and its .twx, and the edited coach spec the switch reason named, so the Modernizer carries its edits over (inspect_coaches previous) instead of redoing them.

step.action: Read the requirement and the example spec
step.details: Read app-specs/example-equipment-request.json for the spec shape and the baw-app-builder skill for the rules. Ask only when the requirement does not say what a screen collects. When the user attaches or names screenshots, follow the screenshot-to-app skill instead: view_image opens a screenshot file in the project.

Every app needs a theme file. Reuse one the user names; otherwise ask the user to describe the look (colours, font, corners, product name, logo) and write work/NAME.theme.json with the app-theme skill. From screenshots, read the look from the image instead of asking, except the logo: never crop it unasked. Never make up a look without asking.

Call list_apps once and pick an unused acronym. For a new app, ask at the design stop which installed app to match (create_app base) or whether to use the built-in template. When list_apps reports that no BAW server is configured, ask the user for the acronym and build without a server.

phase.name: step_by_step
phase.description: When the requirement document's headings name the build steps (for example Process, a Business Object, a Coach View, a Client-Side Human Service, UI Validations, Expected Outcome), or the user asks to build step by step: build it one heading at a time and check with the user after each one

steps.step: After the initialization steps (requirement, screenshots, look, acronym), make a to-do list with one item per heading, in the document's order and with the document's names (e.g. "1. Process", "2. General Information Business Object"). When the last heading is an expected outcome, the last item is "Validate the workflow". Show the list, mark the items that end with an offer to import into BAW (each Coach View item and the Client-Side Human Service item), and say that you stop after each item

Work on one item at a time: write that part of work/ACR.app.json and show only that part, short enough to read in a minute. Process: the process name, the lanes, the human activities in order and the flow (Start → ... → End); an activity that shows the form read-only before it is sent becomes process.review (read-only, Edit on each section, Submit) with "review": false on the spec, never the review page inside the form. Business Object: its name and variable, and a table of every field with the document's data type and whether it is required. Coach View: its name, the business object it binds to, its sections and columns, and the control and label of each field. Client-Side Human Service: its name, the tabs and the View on each, the buttons on each tab, the variables and the data mapping to the process, and the review task. UI Validations: the required fields, the message, the button that stays blocked, and the tab the user is kept on

STOP at the end of every item: mark it done in the to-do list, ask the user to check it and whether to go on to the next item (name it). At a Coach View item and the Client-Side Human Service item, also ask whether to build and import it into BAW first, so the user can check it there. Never start the next item before the user answers. When the user asks for a change, change the spec and show the changed part again

Import to check in BAW: create_app needs a business object and a screen with fields, so the first app that can be built is at the first Coach View item. The Process and Business Object items offer no import (the process is in BAW from the first import on, with its tasks). When the user says yes at the end of an item: write the service as far as the items done so far go (its name and layout, one tab or step per Coach View done, each placing its View; the buttons and the review task come with the Client-Side Human Service item), next to the process. At the first import, ask which installed app to match or the built-in template, and pick the toolkit (the build phase's "Pick the toolkit"); every later import uses the installed app as base and bumps app.snapshot. Then create_app, inspect_coaches, install_app (the user's yes is the import approval for this item; do not ask again), and test_service: the View's "<View> Preview" service at a Coach View item, the form service at the Client-Side Human Service item. Show the screenshots and the run URLs, then STOP again and ask whether to go on to the next item. The import and its test belong to the current item: never run the next item's work with them. When the user says no, go on to the next item without building

UI Validations needs the app in BAW: when no import was made yet, build and ask the import question first (with the template question). After its check: test_service for the form service and show its blocked check (the finishing button blocked while required fields are empty, the messages, the tab shown) with the screenshots, then STOP and ask whether to go on to Validate the workflow. When the user asks for a change, rebuild and install with a new snapshot

Validate the workflow: test_process with the process name (with a draft button, also draft_then_resume), compare the screenshots with the originals when built from screenshots, and report each task, the result and the screenshot folders. Then give the user the Workplace steps to try it, and say that the window closes after the form task and the next task opens from the task list

phase.name: build
phase.description: Design, build, install and test with the baw-app-builder skill

steps.step: When built from screenshots: use only the screenshots the user named; never open or copy other images in their folder unless the user asks. Sample the theme colours from them with image_colors before writing the spec. For the logo, use a logo file the user gave or one already in the project; when there is none, ask at the design stop. Run crop_image only when the user asks for it
Write work/ACR.app.json with "theme" set to the theme file

Every section becomes a reusable View by default (coach-groups skill); never put fields directly on the coach unless the user asks (then "reusableViews": false). Find information that repeats: at least three fields on two or more screens, or groups the user named, become named groups placed on every screen that shows them

When the app stores its form in a table: add a "database" section to the spec ({"table": "public.name", "key": "<field>", "columns": {"<field>": "<column>"}}, see the baw-app-builder skill). Call list_tables("bawexternal") and describe_table first to see which tables exist, and never use a table name that already holds data of another shape. The data source is always jdbc/bawexternal

STOP unless told to go ahead: show the theme, the screens with their sections, fields and buttons, the reusable Views (one per section, and the named groups and where each is placed), the database table, key and columns when there is one, and your assumptions (including anything left out or changed from a screenshot, and any required marker the requirement implies but does not show); ask which installed app to match for a new app; wait for approval before create_app. In a step-by-step build, the stops at the end of each item replace this one

Pick the toolkit: the newest snapshot list_snapshots("ABW") shows that has its work/ABW-SNAPSHOT.twx. When there is none, or the widgets changed since, build_widget_toolkit("builder") with a new snapshot and install_app it
create_app with toolkit_snapshot, then inspect_coaches on the result and check every step

When create_app returns changedInBaw: list the groups someone changed in BAW, ask per group whether to keep BAW's version or replace it with the spec's, and create_app again with replace_groups for the ones to replace (same snapshot)

When create_app returns changedInBawDropped: tell the user those groups, changed in BAW, are not in the new snapshot because the spec no longer builds them (a section renamed, removed or made inline, or a group renamed or removed); to keep one, change the spec back so it builds the group under its earlier name and create_app again; otherwise do nothing (replace_groups does not apply)

With a "database" section, create_app returns database.ddl and database.columns. Run the ddl with run_sql on bawexternal, then describe_table the table and compare it with database.columns (names, types, primary key). When the table already exists with another shape, do not drop or alter it: ask the user whether to use another table name or to change the table. Tell the user that an optional Integer or Decimal field is a text field that accepts only numbers (a blank saves as NULL)
STOP unless told to go ahead: tell the user the app is built and ask whether to import it into BAW; if not, give them the .twx and the import steps and stop
install_app, then test_service for the service (with required fields it also checks the finishing button is blocked while they are empty); look at the screenshots

With a "database" section: test_service with values (a made-up key, e.g. {"Request Number": "R-1"}) fills and submits the form, which saves a row; check the row with run_sql. Then test_service again with the same key in values and press ["Load"]: the form shows the stored row, and an unknown key shows "No record found". Drop only tables you created for the check, and say so

With a "process": test_process with its name and press set to the approval's Send Back label, so the work goes back once before it is approved (with a review instead of an approval, do not press Send Back); look at each task's screenshots

When built from screenshots: view_image each test screenshot, compare it with its original, show the differences and fixes, and after approval fix the spec or the theme file and rebuild and import with a new snapshot until the header, tabs, sections, column placement and widths, fields, controls, required markers, colours and buttons (labels, colours, position) match

phase.name: hand_off
phase.description: When the user asks for a React UI, a modern UI, or to modernize the screens: switch to BAW Coach Modernizer

steps.step: Finish the build phase first, with its stops: the app is built, inspect_coaches has written the coach spec, and the app is installed and tested, or the user chose not to import it, or there is no BAW server

Call switch_mode with mode_id "baw-coach-modernizer" without asking: the user's request is the go-ahead. Never in your first reply of a task (see .bob/rules/baw-mode-routing.md): when the request is the task's first message, call list_files on work/ first. In the reason, give the app name, acronym, installed snapshot, the .twx path, the coach spec path and the theme file, and repeat what the user asked for the UI
When one request asks for both a new app and a React UI, build the app here first, then switch

completion_criteria.criterion: The user approved the design before create_app and was asked before install_app

In a step-by-step build, the to-do list has one item per heading, and the user answered at the end of every item before the next one started, and was offered an import into BAW at each Coach View item and the Client-Side Human Service item
With a "database" section: the table exists with the shape of database.columns, test_service typed the key and pressed Load, and run_sql shows the saved row

The app is installed and test_service reports "ok": true for its service, and test_process reports "ok": true for its workflow when the spec has one; when the user chose not to import it, or without a BAW server, the .twx is built, inspect_coaches shows every step, and the user has the import steps

When built from screenshots, every section, field, control, required marker and button in them is built, or listed under assumptions or not built, and the theme file holds the screenshot's colours, header product name and the logo the user chose
When a React UI was requested, you switched to BAW Coach Modernizer with the app's details
The report lists the app, acronym, theme file, snapshots, run URLs, steps, field counts and screenshot folders
